source.title: Understanding Addition and Subtraction in Transformers
source.authors: P. Quirke; Clement Neo; Fazl Barez

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests whether models across a family implement the same identifiable arithmetic algorithm using circuit search, ablation, and causal patching. It does not reproduce or measure grokking training trajectories.
record.gate_note: The paper reports high held-out accuracy and circuit analyses, but does not measure a chance-to-near-perfect test-accuracy jump after training accuracy saturation, or whether a delay changes with training-set size. Its results on shared circuit structure test V6. Task-accuracy results alone are not rows for the grokking versions.
record.test_reason: The study compares circuits across 46 small transformers varying seed, depth, digit length and operation. It reports that all 27 accurate addition and mixed models share one algorithmic skeleton while implementation details vary, which bears on V6. The setting is new for V6: non-modular n-digit addition and subtraction trained on fresh data each step, a generalizing regime with no grokking trajectory. That makes it T3 rather than T2. It measures no delayed generalization, so V1–V5 and V7 are untested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also conclude that the located circuits are sufficient, not merely present. They add that mixed models reuse addition circuitry polysemantically whether or not initialized from an addition model. They make no claim that frontier LLMs use these mechanisms.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains small transformers on fresh, edge-case-enriched integer addition and subtraction data and analyzes their circuits. It does not use the small fixed modular-arithmetic training regime or measure grokking trajectories.
record.method_sensitivity: Circuit binding, redundancy, timing, and delivery route vary across models; the resolved-carry lag is reported as 2 tokens at 5–6 digits and 3 tokens at 8 digits. The deep causal analysis covers four worked-example models, and the paper notes single-seed results per model and class.
record.problems: Deep causal tests were run on four worked-example models; the wider family result relies on automated map-level search and ablation. The paper reports single-seed results per model and class, and says map depth decreases with model size. It does not measure the grokking behavior or delay addressed by V1–V5 and V7.
record.rows_left_out: Task-accuracy and training-loss results in Sections 4.1 and Tables 5–6 were not included because they do not measure the grokking trajectory or delay, and do not test the identity of the implemented algorithm across models.

untested.parts: No delayed test-accuracy jump or training-set-size dependence measured; training uses fresh data each step.
No tracking of circuit formation over training or progress measures.
No non-algorithmic data and no initialization-scale or weight-norm manipulation.
No LLM pretraining or fine-tuning; the authors explicitly make no transfer claim.
Weight decay fixed at 0.1; no critical dataset size or ungrokking.

Convergence in inaccurate models (17 of 46) is not analyzed. There is no modular-arithmetic or grokking-regime test, few seeds per task, and no wide architecture or hyperparameter sweep beyond 2–3 layers.

missing.what: Sufficiency test: keeping only mapped nodes retains 0.94 of 5-digit addition accuracy (0.89/0.92 on 6/8-digit mixed), versus 0.00 for a random same-size set. This strengthens the identification of the shared algorithm.

The 1-layer 3-head 5-digit addition model (12621 fails/M) uses only the per-digit SA/SC algorithm and fails on cascades. This shows a different, incomplete algorithm at smaller depth, i.e. architecture dependence.
Mixed models show the same skeleton and polysemantic reuse whether trained from scratch or initialized from an addition model.

record.verdict_notes: This is a universality result outside the grokking regime: infinite fresh data, so no memorization phase. Its bearing on V6 is on algorithmic convergence in general, not convergence after grokking. The skeleton search is driven by the authors' derived algorithm. They state a model 'may implement a different valid algorithm', and evidence for alternatives would not be captured. Deep causal evidence is single-seed on four models.

versions.untested_parts: No measurement of the specified delayed test-accuracy rise or how its delay varies with training-set size.
The paper analyzes arithmetic circuits but does not track gradual formation of a generalizing circuit or continuous progress measures that anticipate a grokking jump.
No non-algorithmic datasets or initialization-scale/weight-norm sweep testing grokking-like delays.
No LLM pretraining or fine-tuning on realistic data.
No test of weight decay or low norm as an efficiency account of grokking, critical dataset size, or ungrokking.
The study does not exhaustively vary architectures or hyperparameters, nor establish the same algorithm beyond its specialized arithmetic models and tested settings.
No test of adaptive-optimizer instability or floating-point softmax limits as an explanation for grokking delays.

rows.subject: 27 accurate addition and mixed models (aggregate)
rows.size_stated: 2–3 layers; 3–4 attention heads; models described as ∼10M parameters
rows.stage_stated: trained from scratch or initialized from an addition-only model
rows.operation_detail: Automated search for required subtask nodes, followed by ablation and constraint checks

conditions.value: all 27 accurate addition and mixed models

rows.measure: Presence of the required circuit skeleton and satisfaction of its ordering constraints
rows.value: The same skeleton was found in all 27 accurate addition and mixed models; every required subtask was present at a valid position and every ordering constraint held.
rows.note: Aggregate result reported by the paper; the per-model maps are said to be released.
rows.check: Value is right: same skeleton in all 27 accurate addition and mixed models. The search keeps only nodes that satisfy the authors' own algorithm's constraints, so it tests presence of that skeleton, not whether some other algorithm is also present. Of the 29 accurate models, the 2 accurate subtraction-only models are not covered.

source_check.correct: The 27 accurate addition/mixed models include a four-layer initialized mixed model; the aggregate spans 2–4 layers. The shared-skeleton result is correctly reported.
source_check.locator_found: Sections 4.1.1 and 4.2.1; Table 6, initialized mixed model with attention heads reset every 100 steps.
source_check.problem: The stated 2–3-layer range excludes an accurate four-layer model included in the aggregate.

rows.subject: Four worked-example models (6- and 8-digit addition and mixed)
rows.stage_stated: trained from scratch or initialized from an addition-only model
rows.operation_detail: Activation patching, edge path-patching, and step-function interpolation to test resolved-carry computation
rows.measure: Whether the causal carry computation and its delivery to answer positions follow the proposed circuit
rows.baseline: Same-class controls did not produce the carry-specific answer change.
rows.value: Across all four models, the authors report a consistent picture: the carry is computed and propagated, and toggling only the deciding carry changes exactly the affected answer digit; same-class controls do not.
rows.note: The paper also states that the resolved-carry interface replicates across five addition sizes and on mixed models at both tested sizes.
rows.check: This is causal confirmation in only four worked-example models (6- and 8-digit addition and mixed), single seed each. It bears on V6 only as consistency across those four, not across the family.

rows.subject: Accurate model family (aggregate)
rows.stage_stated: trained from scratch or initialized from an addition-only model
rows.operation_detail: Compared circuit properties across the accurate model family
rows.measure: Variation in implementation details alongside the reported invariant algorithm
rows.value: The paper reports that head assignments, redundancy, timing, and delivery routes vary across models without breaking the algorithm; it also reports that some models compute the logically redundant simple-carry subtask and others omit it.
rows.note: The paper distinguishes the invariant algorithm from varying implementations.
rows.check: The row records variation, not invariance. Head binding, redundancy, timing (2- vs 3-token lag), delivery route and use of the redundant SC subtask all differ across models. The algorithm stays the same but the implementation does not, so 'same identifiable algorithm' holds only at the skeleton level. State should be partial, not observed.

source_check.correct: The accurate family spans 2–4 layers. Implementation variation alone warrants cannot_determine for V6, not partial; the observed shared algorithmic skeleton is recorded in R1.
source_check.problem: The depth range omits a four-layer model, and differing implementations do not establish incomplete convergence to the same algorithm.

statements.correction: Shared algorithmic skeleton across all 27 accurate addition/mixed models; variable head assignments, redundancy, timing, delivery routes and optional SC computation; no demonstrated grokking.
